items.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
items.summary:
For reasons best known to those eyeing the pound signs, Manchester City gave a debut to a special rust-coloured kit in front of a nonplussed crowd. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne.

Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties. Nobody could pretend City were up against crack opposition in a one-paced Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and lack the brio of old, but they simply cannot keep the door shut and could not have quibbled about departing with a defeat.

Continue reading...
items.t: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue

items.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
items.summary:
Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday, this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres.

But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight.

Continue reading...
items.t: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres

items.title: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov
items.summary:
• Opening game ends in draw by repetition

  • Defending champion plays white in Game 2

  • Read our move-by-move report of Game 1

  • Sindarov: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

Indian chess star Gukesh Dommaraju held off Javokhir Sindarov amid a mounting time crisis on Tuesday, drawing the opening game of their eagerly awaited $2.5m world title match in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the picturesque Geneva suburb of Cologny.

After spending more than 36 minutes on a single move and much of the afternoon racing against the clock, the defending champion said the time he invested early helped him play faster as a drawish position sharpened and his minutes dwindled opposite the in-form Uzbek challenger. “When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves,” Gukesh said. “And then the moves after that were pretty easy.”

items.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
items.summary:
This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph, or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions.

On the outside, this is a gladiatorial arena, a giant spaceship parked on Ali Sami Yen complex. But inside there is a poor pitch that began cutting up during the warm-up. John McGinn, one of four changes from Villa’s stalemate with Sunderland on Saturday, gestured towards the turf in frustration after a through ball went awry, but nobody of a Villa persuasion could blame defeat on the surface. As Unai Emery had stated, it was the same for both teams.

Continue reading...

items.title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
items.summary:

  • ‘The way we trained today, I don’t see any complacency’

Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks, insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup.

Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. items.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
items.summary:
For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich

When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow.

More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can…
items.t: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing

Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad

This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.

Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.”

items.t: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’

items.title: Steve Smith toils before falling cheaply on return as Sam Konstas pushes Test claim
items.summary:
• Smith’s Sheffield Shield knock cut short by Michael Neser

  • Opener Konstas pushes claims for Test recall with 42 from 86 balls

Steve Smith has fallen cheaply in his batting comeback, making a laborious 12 for NSW against Queensland in their Sheffield Shield clash.

Smith hadn’t played a innings since 22 October, when he battled a neck injury in Australia’s second Test in South Africa. The star batsman returned for NSW ahead of Australia’s first Test against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth.

items.title: Game over? How playing Grand Theft Auto VI is affecting elite athletes’ performances | Sean Ingle
items.summary:
Burning the midnight oil playing video games is not ideal preparation for professional sport – but it’s not all bad

“They miss games, the cheque’s still clearing. And you’re trying to tell me they got this kind of addiction to a video game that they sitting there with their thumbs looking like Donald Trump?” That was ESPN’s Stephen A Smith, one of the US’s most provocative and influential sports pundits, spitting fire and fury last week after hearing that so many NBA and NFL stars were absorbed in Grand Theft Auto VI.

Smith was hardly an outlier. Other pundits, as well as some Manchester United fans, also questioned Bryan Mbeumo’s focus and professionalism after he posted an image of GTA VI and the word “historique” after midnight on Thursday. Meanwhile before last weekend’s Premier League games, the Odd Sport social media account predicted that Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City would all lose. Why? Because their younger squads might be more focused on Vice City than their opponents, and therefore play with less intensity as a result. By Monday that forecast had been liked tens of thousands of times.

items.title: ‘This isn’t F1’: Max Verstappen criticises overtake-heavy Las Vegas Grand Prix
items.summary:
• Red Bull driver says race ‘isn’t how it should be’

  • Race in Nevada featured 352 overtakes

Max Verstappen has said his outstanding victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday was not really true to the spirit of Formula One and how he wants to race.

Verstappen took a remarkable win, defending his lead and retaking it time and time again after it changed hands 35 times in a race dominated by the cars slipstreaming each other.
